# EtlKit

> EtlKit is a free, open-source (MIT) ETL library and data integration toolbox for .NET.
> Data pipelines are written in C# (or declared in XML) from source, transformation and
> destination components that run on TPL Dataflow, plus control-flow tasks for one-line DDL
> and SQL. Core packages target .NET Standard 2.0. It continues the open-source 1.x line of
> ETLBox by Andreas Lennartz; in 2.0 the packages were renamed from EtlBox.Classic to EtlKit.

- Website: https://www.etlkit.org/
- Source: https://github.com/etlkit/etlkit
- NuGet: https://www.nuget.org/packages?q=Owner%3AEtlKit
- API reference: https://etlkit.github.io/etlkit/
- License: MIT

## When to use EtlKit

- You write .NET and want ETL/ELT logic in C#, reviewed, unit-tested and deployed with the rest
  of your code — an alternative to SSIS packages.
- You move data between relational databases, files and message queues inside your own app,
  worker service or console job; there is no server to install.
- You need bulk loads, table synchronisation (upsert with deletions), file imports with
  bad-row capture, or long-running ingestion from Kafka, MongoDB change streams or a
  PostgreSQL table.

Pick something else when you need a visual designer (SSIS), hundreds of ready-made SaaS
connectors with a UI (Airbyte), a standalone data-routing server (Apache NiFi), or vendor
support for the closed-source ETLBox 2.x+. For a single one-off query, plain ADO.NET or Dapper
is enough.

## Install

```
dotnet add package EtlKit
```

`EtlKit` is the only package a basic setup needs. Add-on packages are opt-in:

- `EtlKit.ClickHouse` — ClickHouse connection manager (.NET Standard 2.1)
- `EtlKit.Kafka` — `KafkaJsonSource<T>` consumer, `KafkaTransformation` producer
- `EtlKit.RabbitMq` — `RabbitMqTransformation` publisher
- `EtlKit.MongoDB` — `MongoChangeStreamSource<T>` (net6.0+, replica set required)
- `EtlKit.PostgresStreaming` — `PostgresXminTailSource<T>` (PostgreSQL 13+)
- `EtlKit.Rest` — `RestTransformation`, an HTTP call per row
- `EtlKit.AI` — `AIBatchTransformation` for OpenAI-compatible chat models
- `EtlKit.Json` — `JsonTransformation` (JSONPath)
- `EtlKit.Scripting` — `ScriptedRowTransformation` (C# expressions compiled with Roslyn)
- `EtlKit.DynamicLinq` — `ExpressionRowFiltration` (Dynamic LINQ string filters)
- `EtlKit.Serialization` — XML pipeline configuration via `DataFlowXmlReader`
- `EtlKit.Logging.Database` — writes ETL log events to a database table

`EtlKit.Common` and `EtlKit.Primitives` are dependencies; do not reference them directly.

## Data flow in three steps

1. Create the components.
2. Connect them with `LinkTo()`. It returns the target, so calls chain; pass a `Predicate<T>`
   to route rows to different destinations.
3. Run the source and wait for every destination: `source.Execute()` + `dest.Wait()`, or
   `await source.ExecuteAsync()` + `await dest.Completion`. There is no `WaitAsync()` and no
   `Network` class.

```csharp
using EtlKit.Common.DataFlow;   // RowTransformation
using EtlKit.ConnectionManager; // SqlConnectionManager, PostgresConnectionManager, ...
using EtlKit.DataFlow;          // CsvSource, DbDestination, ...

var conn   = new SqlConnectionManager("Data Source=.;Initial Catalog=demo;Integrated Security=SSPI;");
var source = new CsvSource<Order>("orders.csv");
var clean  = new RowTransformation<Order>(o => { o.Email = o.Email.Trim(); return o; });
var dest   = new DbDestination<Order>(conn, "Orders");

source.LinkTo(clean).LinkTo(dest);

await source.ExecuteAsync();
await dest.Completion;
```

Rows are POCOs (properties map to columns by name, or via `[ColumnMap("col")]`),
`ExpandoObject` (non-generic component variants such as `CsvSource`, `DbDestination`), or
`string[]` / `object[]`.

Rows that throw in a component can be routed instead of failing the flow:
`component.LinkErrorTo(errorDest)` emits `EtlKitError` rows (ErrorText, ReportTime, Exception,
RecordAsJson); `CreateErrorTableTask` creates a table for them.

## Connectors

Relational databases use the generic `DbSource<T>` / `DbDestination<T>` with a connection
manager. `DbDestination` writes in batches (default 1000 rows) using the fastest path per
database.

| Connector | Source | Destination | Streaming | Resumable | Bulk write | Package |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SQL Server (`SqlConnectionManager`) | yes | yes | no | no | SqlBulkCopy | EtlKit |
| PostgreSQL (`PostgresConnectionManager`) | yes | yes | no | no | binary COPY | EtlKit |
| PostgreSQL table tail (`PostgresXminTailSource<T>`) | yes | no | polling | checkpoint | — | EtlKit.PostgresStreaming |
| MySQL (`MySqlConnectionManager`) | yes | yes | no | no | multi-row INSERT | EtlKit |
| SQLite (`SQLiteConnectionManager`) | yes | yes | no | no | INSERTs in one transaction | EtlKit |
| ClickHouse (`ClickHouseConnectionManager`) | yes | yes | no | no | INSERT … FORMAT CSV | EtlKit.ClickHouse |
| MS Access (`AccessOdbcConnectionManager`) | yes | yes | no | no | multi-row INSERT | EtlKit |
| MongoDB (`MongoChangeStreamSource<T>`) | yes | no | change streams | resume token | — | EtlKit.MongoDB |
| Kafka (`KafkaJsonSource<T>`, `KafkaTransformation`) | yes | producer | yes | consumer-group offsets | batched producer | EtlKit.Kafka |
| RabbitMQ (`RabbitMqTransformation`) | no | publish | no | no | — | EtlKit.RabbitMq |
| CSV / JSON / XML (`CsvSource<T>`, `JsonDestination<T>`, ...) | yes | yes | no | no | streamed | EtlKit |
| Excel (`ExcelSource<T>`) | yes | no | no | no | — | EtlKit |
| HTTP (`ResourceType.Http` on file components, `RestTransformation`) | yes | yes | no | no | — | EtlKit, EtlKit.Rest |
| .NET collections (`MemorySource<T>`, `MemoryDestination<T>`) | yes | yes | no | no | — | EtlKit |
| Anything else (`CustomSource<T>`, `CustomDestination<T>`) | yes | yes | — | — | — | EtlKit |

Streaming sources run until their `CancellationToken` is cancelled:
`source.Execute(cancellationToken)`. Resumable sources load their position from an
`ICheckpointStore<TPosition>` (ready-made: `DbCheckpointStore<TPosition>`); a terminal
`CheckpointWriter<TInput, TPosition>` commits it after the destination has written the row.
Delivery is at-least-once, so destinations should be idempotent; committing inside the
destination's own transaction gives effective exactly-once.

`PostgresXminTailSource<T>` polls by transaction ID (xmin frontier). It sees inserts and
updates but not deletes, and it is not logical-replication CDC.

## Transformations

- Non-blocking: `RowTransformation`, `RowBatchTransformation`, `Aggregation`
  (`[GroupColumn]`, `[AggregateColumn]`), `MergeJoin`, `Multicast`, `RowDuplication`,
  `RowMultiplication`, `RowFiltration`, `ExpressionRowFiltration`, `ScriptedRowTransformation`,
  `SqlQueryTransformation`, `SqlCommandTransformation`, `JsonTransformation`,
  `RestTransformation`, `AIBatchTransformation`, `KafkaTransformation`, `RabbitMqTransformation`.
- Partially blocking (hold the lookup side in memory): `LookupTransformation`, `CrossJoin`.
- Blocking (hold all rows): `BlockTransformation`, `Sort`.

`DbMerge<T>` synchronises a destination table with the incoming rows: it marks each row as
insert, update, delete or unchanged using `[IdColumn]`, `[CompareColumn]` and `[DeleteColumn]`
(or `MergeableRow`). Modes: `Full`, `NoDeletions`, `Delta`. Tested on SQL Server, PostgreSQL,
MySQL, SQLite and ClickHouse.

## Control flow

One-line tasks over any connection manager, in `EtlKit.ControlFlow`: `SqlTask.ExecuteNonQuery`,
`SqlTask.ExecuteReader`, `CreateTableTask.Create`, `DropTableTask`, `IfTableOrViewExistsTask`,
`RowCountTask.Count`, `TruncateTableTask`, `CreateIndexTask`, `CreateViewTask`,
`CreateProcedureTask`, and more. Set `ControlFlow.DefaultDbConnection` to omit the connection.

Logging uses Microsoft.Extensions.Logging: set `ControlFlow.LoggerFactory` or inject `ILogger<T>`
into a component.

## XML pipelines

`EtlKit.Serialization` builds a data flow from XML at runtime. Element names are C# class names,
child elements are property names. `<LinkTo>` connects a component to the next; `<Pipeline>`
lists steps in order (the first may be a source) and a `<LinkTo>` inside it routes the output.
The root element is your own class implementing `IDataFlow` (for example `EtlDataFlowStep`).
Delegate-based components such as `RowTransformation` cannot be expressed in XML; use
`ExpressionRowFiltration`, `ScriptedRowTransformation`, `RestTransformation` or
`AIBatchTransformation`.

```xml
<EtlDataFlowStep>
    <Pipeline>
        <MemorySource />
        <ExpressionRowFiltration>
            <FilterExpression>Amount &gt; 0</FilterExpression>
        </ExpressionRowFiltration>
        <LinkTo>
            <DbDestination>
                <ConnectionManager type="SqlConnectionManager">
                    <ConnectionString>Data Source=.;Initial Catalog=demo;Integrated Security=SSPI;</ConnectionString>
                </ConnectionManager>
                <TableName>orders</TableName>
            </DbDestination>
        </LinkTo>
    </Pipeline>
</EtlDataFlowStep>
```

```csharp
var step = DataFlowXmlReader.Deserialize<EtlDataFlowStep>(xml, new ErrorLogDestination());
```
